text.en: Verbal reduplication in Hokkaido Ainu is a productive word-formation process that serves primarily to express repetition or duration of an action or phenomenon ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verb-reduplication-expresses-action-plurality⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-verb-is-mostly-used-to⟧. Nakagawa analyses it as expressing lexical aspect rather than the grammatical category of number, a characterisation that differs in level of analysis from accounts that treat it as marking plurality of action ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verb-reduplication-expresses-action-plurality⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verb-reduplication-expresses-lexical-aspect⟧. Three structural types are distinguished: root reduplication, partial stem reduplication, and full stem reduplication ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verbal-reduplication-in-ainu-includes-root-reduplication-partial⟧. Root reduplication expresses repetition of action for transitive verbs and repetition of change of state or a high degree of state for intransitive verbs ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-verbal-root-expresses-iterative-aspect⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verb-root-reduplication-indicates-repetition-of-action-for⟧; Satō further specifies that root-reduplicated verbs such as *yas-yas-ke* denote an action occurring irregularly in various places, with the range or degree of the action being small and affecting only a part ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verbs-formed-by-reduplicating-a-root-element-express⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-verbal-root-e-g-yas⟧. Partial stem reduplication — reduplication of the portion of the root following the initial consonant, or of the final syllable of the verb stem — expresses continuative aspect and, more precisely, the continuation of the result after an action is performed ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-portion-of-the-root-following⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-final-syllable-of-the-verb⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--partial-stem-reduplication-of-verbs-expresses-the-continuation⟧; the form *sik-mak-ak-a* is cited as an instance of this pattern ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-verbal-root-e-g-yas⟧. Full stem reduplication expresses repetition of action or change of state, continuation of action, or a high degree of state ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--full-reduplication-of-a-verb-or-adjective-stem⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--full-stem-reduplication-of-verbs-expresses-repetition-of⟧, and Satō associates complete reduplication of the word, as in *yaske-yaske*, with an action occurring to a full degree ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--when-an-entire-word-is-reduplicated-rather-than⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-verbal-root-e-g-yas⟧. Root reduplication and partial stem reduplication are in principle restricted to V/*-pa* type verbs, whereas full stem reduplication is found on various verb types ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-root-or-part-of-the⟧. Reduplication of adverbs or particles indicates emphasis ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-adverbs-or-particles-indicates-emphasis⟧, and reduplication plays an important role in verb word formation generally, while nouns formed by reduplication — such as *ramram* 'scales' and *taktak* 'lump' — are not very common ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-plays-an-important-role-in-verb-word⟧. Vowel reduplication also occurs commonly in derivational morphology more broadly ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--in-ainu-word-formation-roots-may-undergo-reduplication⟧. In the Sakhalin variety, reduplication of verb stems expresses repetition of an action or a high degree of a quality ⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-verb-stems-expresses-repetition-of-an⟧.
text.ja: 北海道アイヌ語における動詞の重複は、動作や現象の反復または継続を示すために主として用いられる生産的な語形成の手段である⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verb-reduplication-expresses-action-plurality⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-verb-is-mostly-used-to⟧。中川はこれを数のカテゴリーではなく語彙的アスペクトを表す手段として分析しており、この記述は動作の複数性を表すとする分析と分析レベルの点で異なる⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verb-reduplication-expresses-action-plurality⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verb-reduplication-expresses-lexical-aspect⟧。構造的には、語根の重複、語幹の一部の重複、語幹全体の重複の三種類が区別される⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verbal-reduplication-in-ainu-includes-root-reduplication-partial⟧。語根の重複は、他動詞では動作の反復を、自動詞では状態変化の反復または状態の程度が大きいことを表し⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-verbal-root-expresses-iterative-aspect⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verb-root-reduplication-indicates-repetition-of-action-for⟧、佐藤はさらに*yas-yas-ke*のような語根重複動詞が行為のあちこちで不規則に行われることを表し、その範囲や程度が小さく一部分にしか及ばないと指摘する⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--verbs-formed-by-reduplicating-a-root-element-express⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-verbal-root-e-g-yas⟧。語幹の一部の重複——語根の頭音以外の部分の重複または語幹の最後の音節の重複——は持続態を表し、より具体的には動作が行われた後の結果の持続を表す⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-portion-of-the-root-following⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-final-syllable-of-the-verb⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--partial-stem-reduplication-of-verbs-expresses-the-continuation⟧；*sik-mak-ak-a*がこのパターンの例として挙げられる⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-verbal-root-e-g-yas⟧。語幹全体の重複は動作・状態変化の反復、動作の継続、または状態の程度が大きいことを表し⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--full-reduplication-of-a-verb-or-adjective-stem⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--full-stem-reduplication-of-verbs-expresses-repetition-of⟧、佐藤は*yaske-yaske*のような語の完全な重複を行為が完全な程度に行われることと関連付ける⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--when-an-entire-word-is-reduplicated-rather-than⟧⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-verbal-root-e-g-yas⟧。語根の重複および語幹の一部の重複は原則的にV/*-pa*型の動詞に限られるが、語幹全体の重複はいろいろな動詞に見られる⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-the-root-or-part-of-the⟧。副詞または助詞の重複は強調を表し⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-adverbs-or-particles-indicates-emphasis⟧、重複は動詞の語形成の手段として重要な役割を果たす一方、*ramram*「鱗」や*taktak*「塊」のような重複によって作られた名詞の例はさほど多くない⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-plays-an-important-role-in-verb-word⟧。母音の重複は語派生においても一般的に見られる⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--in-ainu-word-formation-roots-may-undergo-reduplication⟧。樺太方言では、動詞語幹の重複形は動作の反復や程度の高いことを表す⟦claim:phon/reduplication-phonology-rule-interaction--reduplication-of-verb-stems-expresses-repetition-of-an⟧。
